pieces.title: Practice leave-behind: switching eligible patients to KEYTRUDA QLEX
pieces.body: KEYTRUDA QLEX (pembrolizumab and berahyaluronidase alfa) is approved in the U.S. in the solid tumor indications approved for KEYTRUDA. Every-3-week dose: 395 mg injected subcutaneously over 1 minute. Patients on IV pembrolizumab can switch at their next scheduled dose. In a 147-patient crossover study, 65% of 118 respondents preferred subcutaneous dosing, mostly citing less time in clinic; 32% preferred IV. IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION, same type size and placement as the benefit text: Contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity to berahyaluronidase alfa, hyaluronidase or any excipient. Immune-mediated adverse reactions, which may be severe or fatal, can occur in any organ system. With chemotherapy, serious adverse reactions occurred in 39% and fatal adverse reactions in 10% of patients; the most common adverse reactions were nausea (25%), fatigue (25%) and musculoskeletal pain (21%). See full Prescribing Information. No comparison with other PD-1 or PD-L1 products is made.

move: Re-price U.S. Keytruda Qlex so its Medicare Part B payment per dose moves from 3.6% above IV pembrolizumab to 5% below it, accepting about $796M of forgone Qlex revenue over 24 months, to make Qlex the cheaper choice for payers and patients' coinsurance before biosimilars reach IV in December 2028.

cost.math: 1) Q2 2026 Medicare per-dose payment: Qlex 395 mg x $32.129/mg = $12,691 [tables/partb_asp_quarterly.csv#388]; IV 200 mg x $61.251/mg = $12,250 [tables/partb_asp_quarterly.csv#385]; Qlex premium = 3.6%. 2) Price cut to reach 5% below IV = 1 - 0.95/1.036 = 8.3% [assumption: net price moves with the payment limit]. 3) Qlex share path 7.9% [MRK:10q_2026Q2.md p.28] to 40% straight-line, average 23.9% [assumption]; U.S. family run-rate $20,024M [assumption, Q2 2026 x4]; Qlex sales over 24 months = 20,024 x 23.9% x 2 = $9,590M. 4) Forgone revenue = 9,590 x 8.3% = $796M.
